 B.A.No.5963 OF 2012  ---------------------------------
 Dated this the 6th day of September, 2012  ORDER

This is an application for bail under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure filed by accused Nos.1 to 4 in Crime No.732 of 2012 of Museum Police Station, Thiruvananthapuram for having committed offences under Sections 328, 304 and 34 IPC read with 59(III) of the Food Safety &
Standards Act 2006.

2. The prosecution allegation appears is that the first petitioner is the proprietor of a hotel by name "Salwa Cafe" and the others are employees who cooks putrefied chicken and served to continue causing ill health to some persons and also causing death of one person.
The petitioners are in custody from 18.7.2012 onwards.
3. The learned counsel for the petitioners points out that petitioners are innocent and have been falsely implicated with ulterior motive.
At any rate, it is pointed out that since the investigation has progressed to a good extent, their continued custody is unnecessary.
They expressed their willings to abide by any conditions if bail is granted.
4. The learned Public Prosecutor very vehemently opposed the petition.

As far as the first petitioner is concerned, it is pointed out that he was involved in similar incident for the year 2007 and pointed out that the investigation is yet to be completed and therefore, petitioners may not be granted bail.
5. The allegation is that 1st petitioner and others cookes putrefied chicken and served to several customers causing ill health to some persons and also causing death of one person.
From the materials now available it is difficult to come to affirm that petitioners are innocent.

sentences.text: The petitioners are innocent.
Whatever that be so, the petitioners have been in custody since 18.7.2012 onwards.

In the above circumstances, the petition is allowed as follows:
1) The petitioners shall be released on bail on each of them executing a bond for Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty five Thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum each to the satisfaction of the JFCM-III, Thiruvananthapuram.
2) The learned Magistrate shall ensure the identity of the sureties and veracity of the tax receipts produced by the sureties.
3) The petitioners shall report before the Investigating Officer on every Friday between 10 am and 11 am till final report is laid.
4) The petitioners shall not tamper or attempt to tamper with the evidence or influence or try to influence the witnesses.
5) If any of the condition is violated, the bail granted shall stand cancelled, and the JFCM concerned, on being satisfied of the said fact, may take such proceedings as are available to him in law.
P.BHAVADASAN, JUDGE cms Abdul Khaddar vs The State Of Kerala on 6 September, 2012 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91794200/
